inputs.text: ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.

fields.description: Fog warning: thick fog is expected in western regions of the UAE. Visibility may drop to zero at times from 21:30 tonight (Tue 17 Feb) until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. Drive with extreme caution. More: https://alerts.example.ae
fields.headline: Fog warning: visibility may drop to zero in western regions tonight until 10:00 Wednesday
fields.instruction: If you drive, slow down, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and follow the modified speed limits. Follow all traffic safety guidelines.
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was excluded on that basis.
No specific roads, towns or emirates are named, because the NCM statement only says 'several western regions of the UAE'.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set severity to Moderate and certainty to Likely because NCM describes 'potential' fog, but says visibility may fall to zero. Please confirm whether you want Severe instead. Also check that the operator's 'Western region (demo zone)' matches NCM's 'several western regions'.

payload.summary: Times (21:30 Tue 17 Feb to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb), place (western regions), hazard (fog and low visibility, possibly zero) and Likely/Moderate/Expected all match the NCM bulletin. One problem: the description says thick fog is expected across western regions. The bulletin only warns of potential fog formation and mentions thick fog for some areas.

no_basis.concern: The register entry is a demo authority ('stands in for the real issuer') and the area codes are a 'DEMO-ZONE'. Yet the context is a real event, the console is live and the status is Actual. A person may want to confirm that live dissemination from a demo identity is intended.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause restricting stand-in or demo issuers from sending Actual alerts on a live console. None was found among the clauses shown.

objections.fix: Cut each text to fit one page. That means about 93 characters for English in GSM-7 and about 41 characters for Arabic in UCS-2, since one page is 82 usable octets. Keep only the hazard, area, time and action. Drop the long date phrasing and possibly the URL, or shorten them. If a one-page Arabic UCS-2 text cannot carry the essential content, a person should decide whether to accept it.
objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE handset requirement of a single cell broadcast page. English (218 characters, GSM-7) takes 3 pages and Arabic (228 characters, UCS-2) takes 6.

objections.issue: The protective action ('Drive with extreme caution' / 'قُد بحذر شديد') sits near the end of both texts. On a multi-page delivery the first page carries only the hazard and timing, not the action.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present and the encodings are appropriate (GSM-7 for English, UCS-2 for Arabic). However, both messages break the UAE 1-page limit: English runs to 3 pages and Arabic to 6. The protective action also appears only at the end of each message, so it is not on the first page. The drafter can fix both problems by rewriting much shorter texts that lead with the hazard and the action.

payload.summary: Meaning matches in all three fields. The hazard (thick fog, visibility may drop to zero), the place (western regions of the UAE), and the times (21:30 tonight, Tue 17 Feb, until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb) are the same in both languages. The headline's 'tonight until 10:00 Wednesday' also matches, and the URL is unchanged. The protective actions are carried over faithfully: drive with extreme caution (قُد بحذر شديد), slow down, keep a safe distance, follow the modified speed limits, and follow traffic safety guidelines. I found no meaning differences. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named person who reads Arabic must still verify and approve it before release; this review does not replace that.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. The English text fits one GSM-7 page. The Arabic text is 95 characters in UCS-2, which takes 3 pages.
